title: Why Was the Shopping Cart Invented?
description:
In 1937 an Oklahoma grocer built the first shopping cart so people would buy more, then had to hire models to push it because no one would touch it.
#shoppingcart #grocery #business #shorts

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine (Dec 2025); History.com; Invention & Technology (American Heritage); The Jewish Press (2019); Wikipedia (Sylvan Goldman); Tasting Table and Foodie, citing Martin Lindstrom on TODAY
Photos: coolmikeol, rich701, qmnonic, Seattle Municipal Archives, Stephan Rosger, martinhoward, bfishadow, Images_of_Money, Polycart, Håkan Dahlström, r.nial.bradshaw (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
tags: how stores make you spend more
first_comment: Be honest: do you grab a cart or a basket for a "quick" grocery run? 🛒

scenes.say: Your grocery cart was invented to make you spend more. And at first, nobody would touch it.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine Dec 2025 (grocer wanted to make it easier for customers to buy more); History.com; Wikipedia

scenes.say: In {1936|nineteen thirty six}, an Oklahoma grocer named Sylvan Goldman noticed a problem.
Shoppers quit buying the moment their baskets got too full or too heavy.
scenes.source: History.com ('Women had a tendency to stop shopping when the baskets became too full or too heavy'); Invention & Technology

scenes.say: So he took a folding chair, put a basket on the seat, and wheels on the legs.
scenes.source: Wikipedia ('found a wooden folding chair and put a basket on the seat and wheels on the legs'); Smithsonian Magazine; History.com

scenes.say: On June {4th|fourth}, {1937|nineteen thirty seven}, he rolled them out at his Humpty Dumpty supermarkets.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine; Wikipedia (June 4, 1937, Humpty Dumpty, Oklahoma City)
Smithsonian Magazine (first cart sat unused); Invention & Technology ('Customers didn't want anything to do with the carts')

scenes.say: Men said pushing a cart was women's work. Women said they'd pushed enough baby strollers.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine ('women's work'; 'grown weary of baby strollers'); Wikipedia; History.com

scenes.say: So Goldman hired models to push carts around the store, pretending to shop.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine ('hired attractive models to shop in the store while confidently pushing the carts'); Wikipedia; History.com (actors); Invention & Technology (people posing as customers)

scenes.say: Smithsonian magazine says that by {1940|nineteen forty}, store owners faced a seven year wait list for carts.

visual.quote: store owners looking to buy new shopping carts reportedly faced a seven-year wait list

scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine Dec 2025 (verbatim, 14 words); The Jewish Press 2019 ('by 1940 had placed prospective purchasers on a seven-year waiting list')

scenes.say: Goldman collected royalties and became a multimillionaire.
scenes.source: Wikipedia ('became a multimillionaire' via royalties); History.com; The Jewish Press

scenes.say: But here's the interesting part. The carts never stopped growing.
scenes.source: Tasting Table (carts 'considerably larger than they used to be'); Foodie 2023

scenes.say: One marketing expert says when stores doubled the size of their carts, people bought {40%|forty percent} more, without even noticing.
scenes.source: Martin Lindstrom on TODAY, as reported by Tasting Table and Foodie (Oct 2023): cart doubled in size, people bought/spent 40% more; Foodie ('whether they realize it or not')

scenes.say: Today, over {20 million|twenty million} carts roll through American stores.
scenes.source: Smithsonian Magazine ('20 million to 25 million shopping carts'); Tasting Table (more than 25 million by 2016)
